weakest_link: Idea 2's per-die KV bandwidth. At $0.095/M it needs about 330–360 GB/s of LPDDR per die, which is a 512-bit bus. That bus must fit in under 170 mm² left over after 691 mm² of SRAM, alongside the compute and SerDes. Even then, LPDDR is 2.2–4.5× short of the required drain time at 200–400 tok/s per user.
flip_test: Floorplan the 858 mm² die and run a cycle-level simulation of 128K-context DSA decode at 200 and 400 tok/s per user on the 527-die system. Include the prefill GPUs, using the measured prefix-cache hit rate. | Idea 2 loses the lead if both of these hold: the 512-bit PHY plus compute cannot fit, or the simulated rate falls below about 1.1× Rubin NVL72 whole-chain cost per token at 200 tok/s. Then Idea 1 leads, or "none" exceeds 55%. If instead the simulation holds at least 1.3× whole-chain cost per token, Idea 2 rises to about 40%.
unknown: Even if Idea 2 is right, two things are unclear. First, whether sparse-attention MoE models of the DeepSeek-V3.2 class stay the dominant workload long enough to amortize a 527-die design tuned to one sparsity pattern. Second, what LPDDR and HBM prices will be in 2027, since every cost ratio here moves by roughly ±30% with them.
